key_idea: If K is too small, linear algebra gives a low-degree polynomial that vanishes on K. Restricting it to each full line in K forces its top homogeneous part to vanish in every direction, which a low-degree polynomial cannot do.
reason: This is the polynomial method in its purest form. A dimension count produces a vanishing polynomial, and restricting it to lines turns the geometric covering condition into an algebraic statement about the leading form, so a hard-looking combinatorial problem falls in a few lines. Nothing can be removed, the key idea was famously unexpected, and once seen the argument is reusable and feels inevitable.
recognized: Dvir's proof of the finite field Kakeya conjecture (polynomial method), in the form with the sharpened binomial constant
